examples.question_text:
Evaluate each expression when $x=5$. Show the substitution step.
(a) $7+4x$
(b) $18-3x$
examples.solution_text:
Replace each $x$ with $5$, then multiply before adding or subtracting.
(a)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}7+4x\\&=7+4(5)\\&=7+20\\&=27\end{aligned}$
(b)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}18-3x\\&=18-3(5)\\&=18-15\\&=3\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Evaluate. Show which value replaces each pronumeral.
(a) $\frac{3a+2b}{4}$ when $a=6$ and $b=-1$
(b) $5p+8q-r$ when $p=4$, $q=\frac12$ and $r=7$
examples.solution_text:
(a) Keep the negative value in brackets and work out the whole numerator before dividing.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{3a+2b}{4}\\&=\frac{3(6)+2(-1)}{4}\\&=\frac{18+(-2)}{4}\\&=\frac{16}{4}\\&=4\end{aligned}$
(b) Replace each pronumeral with its own value.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5p+8q-r\\&=5(4)+8\left(\frac12\right)-(7)\\&=20+4-7\\&=17\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Evaluate both expressions when $x=-4$. Explain why the answers differ.
(a) $2x^2$
(b) $(2x)^2$
examples.solution_text:
(a) Square the value of $x$ before multiplying by $2$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2x^2\\&=2(-4)^2\\&=2(16)\\&=32\end{aligned}$
(b) The brackets make the whole product $2x$ the number being squared.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(2x)^2\\&=(2(-4))^2\\&=(-8)^2\\&=64\end{aligned}$
The power in (a) applies to $x$ only. In (b), it applies to the whole bracket.

examples.question_text: Evaluate $pq$ when $p=7$ and $q=5$. Show the substitution step.
examples.solution_text:
Replace each pronumeral with its own value. Adjacent pronumerals mean multiplication.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}pq\\&=(7)(5)\\&=35\end{aligned}$
